slides.headline: THE 6 AI RULES THAT MAKE CLAUDE STOP GIVING YOU USELESS ANSWERS
slides.image_prompt: Referee whistle and red armband lying on cobalt table with dollar and warning triangle symbols, harsh flash, orange light, film grain.

slides.headline: 1) GIVE AI A ROLE BEFORE YOU ASK ANYTHING
slides.body: Add 'you are a Series A investor who has rejected 400 pitches' and the same model finds deal-breakers instead. Prompt: "You are a [expert role]. Find every problem and rank by how fatal"

slides.headline: 2) ASK FOR THE OPPOSITE AFTER EVERY PLAN
slides.body: Add one line and it finds the 3 assumptions most likely to break your budget before you spend it. Prompt: "Now give me the 3 strongest arguments against everything you just said"
slides.image_prompt: Two printed documents side by side on a desk — left covered in large green checkmarks, right slashed with red X symbols — a hand pushing the rejected sheet forward. Amber and charcoal. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh flash, film grain. Accent: signal red against warm amber.

slides.headline: 3) SAY THE FORMAT BEFORE THE QUESTION
slides.body: Front-load the format and the same question returns something you can paste and use in 5 minutes. Prompt: "Give me [number] [format] about [topic]. Each must include [constraint] and fit in one sentence"

slides.headline: 4) ASK WHAT IT NEEDS BEFORE IT STARTS
slides.body: Ask this before anything else and the quality of the whole session changes. Prompt: "What are the 5 most important things you need from me? Ask me each one"

slides.headline: 5) MAKE IT CHECK ITS OWN WORK
slides.body: Claude writes confident math that is wrong and doesn't flag it. Tell it to check itself and errors surface before they reach anyone else. Prompt: "Find any number that could be wrong. Fix them"
slides.image_prompt: A hand presses a red pen into a printed page — bold red circles around error symbols — a corrected second copy beside it, green marks replacing red. Charcoal and cool green. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh flash, film grain. Accent: signal red against cool charcoal.

slides.headline: 6) TELL CLAUDE WHO YOU ARE AT THE START
slides.body: Claude doesn't know if you're a student or a 50-person company unless you say so. Prompt: "Context: I'm a [role] running a [type of business] with [budget or team size]. Keep everything relevant"

slides.headline: SAVE THIS
slides.body: You will want these the next time Claude gives you something useless. Save this post and try one rule tonight. New AI skills and the biggest AI story, every day on this page

caption:
Swipe through all 6 before you open Claude today. Each one changes what you get back. 🧠

Give AI a role before you ask anything, ask for the counter-argument after every plan, say the format before the question, ask what Claude needs before it starts, make it check its own work, tell it who you are at the start of every session.

Most people type a question and hit send. That gets you the average answer. These rules separate people who actually get results from AI from everyone who hits the same wall every day. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.
